title: Fix Riley Mission Control agent detail on SQLite
description: Agent detail pages on Riley Mission Control fail with 'Agent not found' after the SQLite cutover because agent route/service lookups treat UUID identifiers as strings in a way that is not portable across dialects. Fix the agent API/service path to normalize UUIDs, add regression coverage, and verify the Riley backend serves agent detail successfully.
close_reason: Fixed by normalizing agent UUID lookups for SQLite-compatible agent detail routes, adding regression coverage, and verifying Riley agent detail/activity/boards APIs return 200.

title: Fix Riley Mission Control dashboard fetch failure
description: Dashboard page shows 'Failed to fetch' after the SQLite cutover/reseed. Diagnose the exact failing API call and restore the dashboard on Riley without disturbing the working boards/gateway/agent paths.
close_reason: Dashboard metrics endpoint restored after SQLite cutover

title: Fix bd git hook command mismatch
description: The repo's installed git hooks call 'bd hook', but the current Beads CLI exposes 'bd hooks'. This breaks bd sync, pre-commit, and normal landing workflows unless commits/pushes are forced with --no-verify. Update the hook scripts or CLI invocation so bd sync works normally again.

title: Reconcile Riley Mission Control clone with upstream after manual hotfixes
description: Riley Mission Control is healthy and reseeded again, but the on-box openclaw-mission-control clone has local drift and manual hotfixes applied directly to restore service. Cleanly reconcile Riley's clone with the pushed upstream repo, preserve the local env/runtime wiring, and verify restart from a clean git state.

title: Restore Riley Mission Control state after SQLite cutover
description: Mission Control is healthy again on Riley after decoupling from the 3090-backed Postgres/Redis path, but the new local SQLite database is empty. Recreate or migrate the Riley gateway record, agent records, and starter boards/board groups on the local DB, and decide whether to keep local SQLite or move to a stable local Postgres/Redis host.
close_reason: Restored Riley Mission Control state on the local SQLite database, recreated the Riley gateway and content/media boards, restored the gateway-main and Comfy lead agent records/tokens, and verified both user and agent API paths against the live Riley backend.

title: Fix Riley Mission Control DB connectivity
close_reason: Fixed by moving Riley Mission Control backend off the unreachable 3090 Postgres/Redis path and restarting it on a local SQLite database. Frontend and backend tunnels now answer again, auth works, and the loading failure is gone.
